## 1. Coolant flow rate

The cold-plate outlet temperature is

\[
T_{\text{out}}=35.0+10.0=45.0^\circ\text{C}
\]

By Rule 1.1,

\[
T_{\text{mean}}=\frac{35.0+45.0}{2}=40.0^\circ\text{C}
\]

At \(40^\circ\text{C}\), KryoSol-45 properties are

\[
\rho=1200\ \text{kg/m}^3,\qquad
c_p=2000\ \text{J/(kg·K)}
\]

\[
\mu=2.40\ \text{mPa·s}=0.00240\ \text{Pa·s},\qquad
P_v=22.0\ \text{kPa(abs)}
\]

The required mass flow is

\[
\dot m=\frac{144000}{2000(10.0)}
      =7.20\ \text{kg/s}
\]

Thus,

\[
Q=\frac{\dot m}{\rho}
  =\frac{7.20}{1200}
  =0.00600\ \text{m}^3/\text{s}
\]

\[
\boxed{Q=21.60\ \text{m}^3/\text{h}}
\]

---

## 2. VortaTube selection

Using

\[
v=\frac{Q}{\pi(D/2)^2}
\]

the velocities are:

| Pipe | \(D\) (m) | Velocity (m/s) | Rule 2.1 result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| VT-32 | 0.032 | 7.460 | Fails: \(v>3.20\) |
| VT-40 | 0.040 | 4.775 | Fails: \(v>3.20\) |
| VT-50 | 0.050 | 3.056 | Passes |
| VT-65 | 0.065 | 1.808 | Fails: \(v<2.00\) |

For VT-50,

\[
v=\frac{0.00600}{\pi(0.050/2)^2}
  =3.055775\ \text{m/s}
\]

Therefore,

\[
\boxed{\text{selected pipe}=\text{VT-50}}
\]

Its 850 kPa maximum working pressure is also well above the calculated circuit pressure drop.

### Reynolds number

\[
Re=\frac{\rho vD}{\mu}
\]

\[
Re=
\frac{(1200)(3.055775)(0.050)}{0.00240}
=76394.4
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{Re\approx 7.6394\times10^4}
\]

This is within the specified turbulent range \(4000\leq Re\leq10^5\).

The Darcy friction factor is

\[
f=\frac{0.3164}{Re^{0.25}}
  =\frac{0.3164}{76394.4^{0.25}}
  =0.0190314
\]

The dynamic pressure is

\[
\frac12\rho v^2
=\frac12(1200)(3.055775)^2
=5602.656\ \text{Pa}
=5.602656\ \text{kPa}
\]

### Suction-line pressure drop

\[
\Delta P_s=
\left(f\frac{L_s}{D}+K_s\right)\frac12\rho v^2
\]

\[
\Delta P_s=
\left[(0.0190314)\frac{8.0}{0.050}+2.50\right](5.602656)
\]

\[
\boxed{\Delta P_s=31.067\ \text{kPa}}
\]

### Discharge-return pressure drop

\[
\Delta P_d=
\left[(0.0190314)\frac{72.0}{0.050}+11.50\right](5.602656)
\]

\[
\boxed{\Delta P_d=217.973\ \text{kPa}}
\]

Total piping loss:

\[
\Delta P_{\text{pipe}}
=\Delta P_s+\Delta P_d
=31.067+217.973
\]

\[
\boxed{\Delta P_{\text{pipe}}=249.040\ \text{kPa}}
\]

## 3. Filter selection

The filter must provide 5 μm or finer filtration and pass \(21.60\ \text{m}^3/\text{h}\).

- FC-100: 3 μm, but \(Q_{\max}=18.0\ \text{m}^3/\text{h}\), so it is too small.
- FC-200: 5 μm and adequate flow capacity, but it leads to an invalid pump operating point, as shown below.
- FC-250: 10 μm, so it does not provide the required 5 μm filtration.
- FC-300: 5 μm and \(Q_{\max}=35.0\ \text{m}^3/\text{h}\).

For FC-300,

\[
C_f=0.35,\qquad B_f=0.015
\]

The viscosity and density ratios are

\[
\frac{\mu}{\mu_{\text{ref}}}=2.40,\qquad
\frac{\rho}{\rho_{\text{ref}}}=1.20
\]

Clean pressure drop:

\[
\Delta P_{\text{filter,clean}}
=
0.35(2.40)(21.60)
+
0.015(1.20)(21.60)^2
\]

Laminar term:

\[
0.35(2.40)(21.60)=18.144\ \text{kPa}
\]

Turbulent term:

\[
0.015(1.20)(21.60)^2
=0.018(466.56)
=8.39808\ \text{kPa}
\]

Therefore,

\[
\Delta P_{\text{filter,clean}}
=18.144+8.39808
=26.54208\ \text{kPa}
\]

Applying the fouled-condition factor:

\[
\Delta P_{\text{filter,fouled}}
=2.0(26.54208)
\]

\[
\boxed{\Delta P_{\text{filter,fouled}}=53.084\ \text{kPa}}
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{\text{selected filter}=\text{FC-300}}
\]

### Why FC-200 is not acceptable

For FC-200,

\[
\Delta P_{\text{clean}}
=0.50(2.40)(21.60)+0.025(1.20)(21.60)^2
=39.9168\ \text{kPa}
\]

\[
\Delta P_{\text{fouled}}=79.8336\ \text{kPa}
\]

This would give a system head of approximately \(33.458\) m. VX-200 at 55 Hz provides only \(32.093\) m. At 60 Hz it provides enough head, but its shaft power is approximately \(3.98\) kW and its required cavitation margin is approximately \(3.137\) m versus only \(3.062\) m available. Therefore FC-200 has no valid discrete VFD setting.

The total fouled-condition pressure rise required from the pump is

\Delta P_{\text{sys}}
=
\Delta P_{\text{pipe}}
+\Delta P_{\text{load}}
+\Delta P_{\text{filter,fouled}}
\]

\[
\Delta P_{\text{sys}}
=249.0396+65.0+53.08416
=367.1237\ \text{kPa}
\]

Since

\[
\rho g=(1200)(9.81)=11772\ \text{Pa/m}
=11.772\ \text{kPa/m}
\]

the system head is

\[
H_{\text{sys}}
=\frac{367.1237}{11.772}
=31.186\ \text{m}
\]

\[
\boxed{H_{\text{sys}}=31.186\ \text{m}}
\]

### 2. Fan–sink operating point

\[
Re_{D_h}=\frac{u_{\rm ch}D_h}{\nu}

A_{\rm eff}=0.03225+0.646058

\[

### 5. Thermal resistance and base temperature

The air heat-capacity rate is

\[
\rho_a c_p\dot V
=(1.14)(1007)(0.0380899)
=43.7265\ {\rm W/K}

hA_{\rm eff}

\frac{hA_{\rm eff}}{\rho_a c_p\dot V}

43.7265[1-\exp(-0.67496)]

\[
\boxed{R_{\rm th}=0.047446\ {\rm K/W}}

Mean base temperature:

\[
T_b=T_{in}+Q_{\rm tot}R_{\rm th}
\]

\[
T_b=35.0+720(0.047446)
=69.161\ ^\circ{\rm C}

\[
\boxed{T_b=69.16\ ^\circ{\rm C}}

This satisfies
